source: Halvings are exact on-chain heights; other events pinned at close public estimates.

events.title: The genesis block
events.note: Value then: nothing. Embedded in it: a newspaper headline — 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.'

events.title: The value-overflow bug
events.note: A bug briefly created 184 billion fake coins. Caught and erased within hours — one of only two times the record ever broke.

events.title: 'Bitcoin is dead' — an early obituary
events.note: Declared dead here. The wall has added over 860,000 blocks since.

events.title: Mt. Gox hacked · price −93%
events.note: Price fell 93%. Block time: still ~10 minutes. The price and the machine are different things.

events.title: First halving — 50 → 25 BTC
events.note: The new-coin rate halved, exactly on schedule, with no one deciding it that day.

events.title: The 2013 chain split
events.note: A software glitch split the record for about 6 hours. The second — and last — time it ever broke.

events.title: 2013 top, then −80%
events.note: A furious run to ~$1,150, then a long collapse. Blocks kept arriving throughout.

events.title: Mt. Gox collapses
events.note: The biggest exchange imploded — a company failing, next door to a network that didn't miss a beat.

events.title: 2017 top ~$19,700, then −84%
events.note: The mania everyone remembers. Then the drawdown the wall simply continued through.

events.title: China bans mining (you fired this in Attack 4)
events.note: Half the world's mining went dark. Recovered within months.

events.title: FTX collapses
events.note: Another giant exchange gone overnight. The ledger underneath: uninterrupted.
